_comment: AcreOS MCP Server — Claude Desktop configuration
_endpoint: POST /api/mcp — the ONLY AcreOS MCP endpoint.
_instructions: Add the 'acreos' entry under 'mcpServers' in your Claude Desktop config:
Credential — an ORGANIZATION API KEY, created in AcreOS under
Settings → API keys. It looks like ak_live_… (or ak_test_… ). Copy it when
it is shown; AcreOS stores only its hash and cannot show it again.
The key decides BOTH what you reach and what you can do with it:
• its organization is the only org any tool call can read, and
• its granted SCOPES decide which tools exist for you at all.
A key with no scopes can still call the ungated reads, and is refused
per-tool on everything else — tools/list simply will not show them.
So grant the key the read scopes you actually want Claude to have
Replace acreos.io below if you run AcreOS on your own domain.
_retired: Earlier editions of this file offered two other options. Both are GONE —
if you are still running one, this is why it stopped working:
• 'acreos-http' pointed at https://acreos.fly.dev/mcp with a static
MCP_API_KEY. Founder ruling R-1 (2026-08-11) retired that endpoint:
it accepted per-org keys but never enforced their scopes, so one
credential had two different ladders depending on which URL you used.
Fix: use the entry above with an ak_ organization key. The static
MCP_API_KEY is retired with it and is not accepted anywhere — a
scope-less env secret has nothing to check against a per-tool ladder.
• 'acreos-stdio' ran server/mcp/index.ts as a local subprocess against
DATABASE_URL. That module was the retired endpoint's tool server and
has been deleted. Fix: use the entry above against your dev server.

acreos._comment: Streamable HTTP transport → POST /api/mcp, org + scopes resolved from the key
